{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-oh-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"06b61ea2e3404b00959dd4fb0316ae23d4d841d5824fe360f93c1367770f5f13","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-oh-class-d:lineage:50","source_registry_sha256":"33124b165dc74fabcff4bbcd8fd15db36bbe4a69a10e7def76a9d71752a5128b","source_liveness_sha256":null},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Emergency situations","heading":"Emergency situations — C","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A74
Most newer vehicles have anti-lock braking intended to prevent skidding during a stop; consult the vehicle manual for the proper braking method. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A75
To steer around a hazard, grip the wheel with both hands and steer toward a path avoiding other traffic, then countersteer to straighten and regain control before slowing. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A75
Acceleration may help avoid a crash when another vehicle is about to strike from behind or from the side. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A75
Excessive speed for conditions, an abrupt stop or loss of tire grip can cause a skid. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A75
At the start of a skid, release pressure on the brake or accelerator and steer into the skid. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A75
Treat an inoperative traffic signal as a four-way stop unless a law-enforcement officer is directing traffic, and proceed carefully because others may fail to stop. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A75
If the vehicle leaves the pavement, ease off the accelerator, slow gradually and return to the paved surface when it is safe. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A76
Follow the maintenance schedule recommended in the vehicle owner's manual. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A76
If normal brakes fail, apply the parking brake slowly so the rear wheels do not lock and cause a skid. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A76
If the parking brake does not work after brake failure, the handbook's fallback is to switch off the engine, leave the road and activate emergency flashers. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A76
For uncontrolled acceleration, turn on emergency flashers, select neutral and look for an escape path. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A76
With an uncontrolled accelerator, steer smoothly, brake gradually and pull off the roadway. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A76
After the described controlled exit from an accelerator malfunction, select park and switch the engine off. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A76
A front tire blowout makes the vehicle pull sharply toward the failed tire. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A76
A rear tire blowout causes wobbling, shaking and some pull toward the failed tire. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A76
During a tire blowout, keep a firm steering grip and hold a straight path. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A76
After a tire blowout, avoid braking and reduce speed gradually. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A76
After a blowout, move off the road at a safe place, activate hazards, select park and shut down the engine. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A77
If the engine stops while driving, hold the wheel firmly; steering may become difficult but remains possible. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A77
After engine failure, use steady brake-pedal pressure to slow down and leave the roadway. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A77
After pulling off for engine failure, select park and attempt a restart; if it fails, raise the hood and turn on emergency flashers. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A77
When a vehicle breaks down, move it off the road and away from traffic if possible. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A77
Activate emergency flashers to warn that the vehicle is disabled. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A77
If possible, place emergency flares about two hundred to three hundred feet behind a broken-down vehicle to warn approaching drivers. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A77
The handbook instructs occupants to stay in the vehicle until assistance arrives after a breakdown. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0077]
